# Hero-memory combo affix rolls its two stats independently

- **Status:** ✅ Confirmed
- **Skills affected:** Hero Memories
- **Mechanic tags:** hero-memory, affix, rolling, combo
- **Last verified:** 2026-08-09 by Owner (in-game domain knowledge, 2026-08-09)

## Setup

The Combo Starter / Combo Finisher hero-memory random affix grants TWO stats on one line — '+X% additional Attack and Cast Speed for Combo Starters' AND '+Y% Critical Strike Damage for Combo Finishers' — that roll with DIFFERENT ranges. Owner confirms the two halves roll INDEPENDENTLY in-game (not one shared roll).

## Raw data points

One affix family in _hero_memories random_affixes (uuid 5777798c), identical across Origin/Discipline/Progress; the only hero-memory affix with 2+ ranges. MIXED arity across 4 tiers: T0 (10–12 / 31–40), T1 (7–9 / 25–30) and T2 (5–6 / 20–24) each have TWO ranges (both halves roll); T3 has a FIXED first half (+4%) and only ONE range (15–19% crit dmg). The editor computes the range count PER-TIER, so T0–T2 render two independent inputs and T3 renders one (the fixed +4% speed isn't editable).

## Derived / confirmed formula

Two INDEPENDENT rolls captured via MemorySlotSelection.rolledValues[] (one value per '(lo–hi)' range, in order; a null entry defaults to that range's max). Distinct from the same-range same-stat SHARED-roll case (see affix-combined-line-shared-roll), which is ONE roll.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

Single-range affixes are unchanged (rolledValue path). Compendium import does not yet set rolledValues for this affix (it defaults to each range's max) — minor, deferred. helpers memoryRangeCount/memoryRangeBounds/memoryRangeMax in api/client.ts.

## Implementation (engine model)

WIRED (renderer). MemorySlotSelection gains rolledValues?: (number|null)[] (mirrors the Fate rolledValues pattern). resolveModifier (api/client.ts buildMemoryEffects) and resolveMemoryEffect (HeroTraitShared) fill each range in order from rolledValues; scaleSelValue scales each element (base-slot penalty); sanitizeMemorySlot preserves the array on save/load/import; the creator's AffixRow renders a tier picker + one slider/input per range for multi-range affixes (the single tier-slider can't represent two independent rolls). No build-code/codec change — additive field on the persisted selection, exactly like Fate rolledValues.
